subject: Orchestration: staging windows, enablement slots, and exceptions plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, platform@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-11-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Orchestration: staging windows, enablement slots, and exceptions plan

Team —

We need to lock the staging window schedule and finalise enablement slots for the ACME go-live next month. The vendor kick-off is scheduled 11/18 and we must ensure: 

- A 24-hour warm-up on staging for the dedicated pool (stops: 11/18 04:00 UTC -> 11/19 04:00 UTC)
- Two 1-hour enablement sessions for ACME product & ops (recorded)
- Exception list (security / data-retention asks) surfaced and owners assigned before engineering freeze (11/12 EOD)

Attached is a draft staging_windows.xlsx with proposed slots and a short exceptions_log.csv pulled from the last intake. Action items: 
1) Dev: confirm whether the 24-hour warm-up is sufficient for cache priming and any special migration steps — @dev_patel
2) Enablement: two sessions — one for product owners, one for SRE/ops — propose times and training owners — @evelyn_hart
3) Release: confirm code freeze enforcement date and if any carve-outs needed for emergency hotfixes — @karthik_iyer

ACME platform leads are looped for visibility; please reply with confirmations by EOD 11/09 so I can finalize invites and the rollout checklist.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Program Manager, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: staging_windows.xlsx (spreadsheet), exceptions_log.csv (csv)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, platform@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-11-07T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orchestration: staging windows, enablement slots, and exceptions plan

Marissa —

24-hour warm-up looks fine for cache priming in the common case. A couple of notes:

- If ACME plans large offline indexing jobs during warm-up (e.g., >1B tokens), we should extend to 36h or gate the heavy jobs to post-warm-up.
- We need a short runbook step for KV cache prefill: engineering can run a prefill job but I’ll need 4 hours operational lead-time the day before.
- Carve-outs during freeze: we should allow emergency security patches with a two-person sign-off (engineering + release) and a short post-deploy verification checklist.

I’ll add the prefill step to the staging spreadsheet and mark the owner as infra-prep (Dev).

—Dev
Dev Patel
Lead Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Quoted message:
> On 2027-11-07, Marissa Cole wrote:
> > Action items:
> > 1) Dev: confirm whether the 24-hour warm-up is sufficient for cache priming and any special migration steps — @dev_patel

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, platform@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-11-08T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orchestration: staging windows, enablement slots, and exceptions plan

Marissa / Dev —

I can run the two enablement sessions. Proposed times (ACME in PST):

- Session A (Product owners): 2027-11-19 10:00–11:00 PT — overview + Q&A (recorded)
- Session B (SRE / Ops deep-dive): 2027-11-19 14:00–15:00 PT — hands-on, runbook walk-through

I'll create two calendar invites and a short enablement deck. Can we also get a small list of customer-specific scenarios to include in the SRE session? ACME: can you share 2–3 high-priority runbooks or incident examples?

Also, regarding the exceptions CSV: I recommend owners be marked as either Product Ops or Security. If we need legal sign-off on a retention exception, please loop in Legal.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Manager, Customer Enablement

Attachments: enablement_slots.ics (calendar stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: platform@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-11-09T10:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orchestration: staging windows, enablement slots, and exceptions plan

Quick update on the release side:

- Code freeze confirmed for 2027-11-12 23:59 PT. Only emergency fixes after that with two-person sign-off.
- I approve the 24-hour warm-up but ask we document an explicit rollback plan in case we hit perf regressions during warm-up.
- For exceptions: I’ll take ownership of the triage queue. Please add a "freeze-impact" column to the exceptions_log.csv so we can prioritize.

I’ll coordinate the release window with SRE and send the final gating checklist by 11/10 EOD.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Manager, Release Engineering

Quoted:
> On 2027-11-07, Dev Patel wrote:
> > Carve-outs during freeze: we should allow emergency security patches with a two-person sign-off (engineering + release)...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: platform@acme-corp.com, jessica@cloudpartner.io
Date: 2027-11-09T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orchestration: staging windows, enablement slots, and exceptions plan

Thanks all — final notes and next steps: 

- Dev: please add the prefill step and estimated runtime to staging_windows.xlsx (owner: dev_patel) — due 11/10 12:00 PT.
- Enablement: Evelyn to share invites + deck and confirm scenarios with ACME (owner: evelyn_hart) — invites out by 11/11.
- Release: Karthik to publish the gating checklist and the rollback playbook (owner: karthik_iyer) — due 11/10 EOD.
- Exceptions: I’ll add the freeze-impact column in exceptions_log.csv and assign initial owners; we will triage on 11/10 09:00 PT.

ACME / Jessica: if there are any must-have integration runs or data migration steps that need special handling please flag them in the Drive folder linked below. We plan to finalize the schedule and invites by COB 11/11.

I’ll keep a short decision log in the Confluence page and share the final rollout timeline once the above items land.

Marissa

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-launch-orchestration
